# Optimized buffered-value comparison envelopes and their first-order limits

This note records exactly what follows from the quantitative parameter-continuity
theorem. It gives actual upper comparisons and a finite scalar lower comparison
using the old contact certificate. It does NOT differentiate an optimizer or
interchange infima, halfspace choices, and directional limits.

Use `candidate b2439018eaa1681d`
for the notation and hypotheses. In particular the limiting positive concave
normalized parameter L carries finite actual volume rows rho_i, weights sigma_i,
proper deepest marks Y_i=(p_i,y_i), and raw depth Q strictly below every
b_base(p_i). Keep epsilon fixed. All bodies below are actual compatible positive
families on the same finite base; mass and within-fiber covariance are current.

## 1. Actual upper comparisons need no optimizer derivative

For a specified body path K(t), define

    v(t)=inf_U Q_t(U)/M_t,

where U ranges over positive continuous concave parameters on the current
canonical hull, logarithmically normalized against its actual mixed volume.
For ANY explicitly admissible parameter path U^a_t,

    v(t)<=Q_t(U^a_t)/M_t.                              (1)

If U^a_0=L, then v(0)=Q/M. Consequently

    limsup_(t down 0) [v(t)-v(0)]/t
       <=limsup_(t down 0) [Q_t(U^a_t)/M_t-Q/M]/t.     (2)

One may take the infimum of the RIGHT sides over any prescribed family of
admissible paths. This only uses the separate inequality for every fixed path;
it is not an exchange of an infimum and a limit. For a finite list, an exact
pointwise upper envelope is min_a Q_t(U^a_t)/M_t.

It is also enough to replace Q_t(U^a_t) by a proved covering upper bound.
For example, if actual continued critical groups cover all old deepest fibers
and the off-deepest gap persists, and their raw common masses are

    Q-t ell_i+o(t),       M_t=M-t D+o(t),

then

    limsup [v(t)-Q/M]/t
       <= -min_i(ell_i-beta D)/M,  beta=Q/M.           (3)

Every ell_i must be the actual response of the SAME body/parameter path,
including supporting-facet inverses and all normalization terms. Formula (3)
does not select a different deformation for different groups. It remains only
an upper bound when other critical menus become better after perturbation.

## 2. A finite exact lower comparison from the old certificate

Choose near-minimizing U_t with Q_t(U_t)/M_t<=v(t)+t^2; exact minimizers are
not needed. Along any sequence t down to zero the continuity theorem applies.
Let a common inward homothety of every OLD fiber about its centroid map it
into the current fiber:

    T_t(z,X)=(z,g_z+(1-a_t)(X-g_z)),  a_t->0,
    I_(t,z)=T_t K_z subset K_z(t),  j_t=(1-a_t)^d.

Pushing rho_i gives the actual mark

    Y_i^t=(p_i,(1-a_t)y_i+a_t E_(rho_i)g_Z).           (4)

The integer base stays p_i. This is a pushforward of probability rows, not
an assertion that the generally nonaffine centroid map preserves bodies.

Define the exact logarithmic collar quantity

    xi_t=(1/M) integral_S log[U_t(T_t w)/L(w)] dm
        =-1/(M j_t) sum_z
                integral_(K_z(t) outside I_(t,z)) log U_t dX.    (5)

The second equality follows from current normalization and the common fiber
Jacobian; the collars are ordinary measurable set differences, even for a
signed body motion. Jensen rowwise and then logarithmically gives

    sum_i sigma_i log[U_t(Y_i^t)/L_i]>=xi_t.           (6)

For a positive scalar s, let B_i(t,s) be the ACTUAL buffered depth at Y_i^t
when its parameter value is s. The rest of a parameter function does not enter
this value: its buffer is [s E_(K_(t,p_i))(y_i^t)/M_t]^(1/N), with the actual
covariance norm. Include pure-base caps as usual.

For all small t there is a common interval J of raw depths about Q, lying
strictly below all current b_base(p_i), on which a unique positive scalar
s_i(t,q) satisfies

    B_i(t,s_i(t,q))=q.                                (7)

Here is why no smooth inverse is assumed. On each compact positive scalar
interval B_i is continuous by the uniform all-direction slab estimate.
Whenever its value is below atomic depth, increasing s strictly increases the
depth: apply the attained-new-cap proper-own-strip argument. At t=0 the value
at s=0 is strictly below Q, since the positive old buffer can be removed from
an old proper minimizing cap. At sufficiently large s every own trace is full,
so whole-fiber capture bounds all nonvertical caps below by atomic depth.
Thus B_i reaches atomic depth. These properties and fixed-scalar continuity
under body perturbations give (7), its strict monotonicity in q, and continuous
convergence of these inverses near q=Q. In particular s_i(0,Q)=L_i.

Put

    H_t(q)=sum_i sigma_i log[s_i(t,q)/L_i].             (8)

It is continuous and strictly increasing on J. For a near-minimizing parameter
and q_t=Q_t(U_t), every old pushed mark has depth at most q_t, so
U_t(Y_i^t)<=s_i(t,q_t). Equations (6) and (8) give the exact inequality

    H_t(q_t)>=xi_t.                                  (9)

For small t, q_t is in J and xi_t->0 by the continuity theorem. Hence, writing
chi_t for the local inverse of H_t,

    Q_t(U_t)>=chi_t(xi_t).                            (10)

This is stronger than the simpler valid estimate
Q_t(U_t)>=min_i B_i(t,L_i exp(xi_t)). It retains the certificate weights and
all proper source marks simultaneously. It is a scalar comparison built from
actual all-halfspace depths, not a claimed first-order response formula.

## 3. One-sided collar control, including the boundary

The continuity proof supplies uniform sampled maxima U_t<=B, with B>=1.
For the LOWER comparison only an upper bound on log U_t is needed. Hence the
exact identity (5) immediately gives

    xi_t>=-h_t log B/(M j_t),                         (11)

where h_t is the total collar volume. The uniform-integrability estimate
O(h_t(1+|log h_t|)) from the stability proof controls the ABSOLUTE error, but
is unnecessary here. In particular a Hausdorff O(t) body path and a_t=O(t)
give h_t=O(t) and an O(t) one-sided lower bound, without any positive lower
bound on the varying parameters at the boundary.

There is a sharper one-sided limit. Choose any continuous positive reference
extension L_ref,t on the current sampled fibers such that
L_ref,t(w_t)->L(w) whenever sampled w_t->w in S. For example, independently
on each fiber use L(z,projection_(K_z) X). This is just a comparison function;
no concavity or parameter admissibility of this extension is needed. Then

    sup_(S_t) [U_t-L_ref,t]_+ ->0.                    (12)

Proof. Otherwise, along a fixed-base subsequence take w_t->x in a limiting
fiber and U_t(w_t) converging to a value above L(x), using the uniform maximum
bound. If x is interior this contradicts interior convergence. Otherwise fix
an interior point g and 0<s<1. The points (1-s)g+s w_t lie in a fixed interior
core for small t. Concavity implies

    U_t(w_t)<=[U_t((1-s)g+s w_t)-(1-s)U_t(g)]/s.

Pass to the limit using interior convergence, then let s increase to one.
Continuity of L at the old boundary gives limsup U_t(w_t)<=L(x), again a
contradiction. This excludes upward boundary spikes; it does not exclude the
downward layers in Section 5.

The reference functions have a common positive floor, so (12) implies
log U_t<=log L_ref,t+o(1) uniformly. Therefore

    xi_t >= -1/(M j_t) sum_z integral_(collar_z) log L_ref,t
                    +o(h_t).                        (13)

This is a one-sided statement and does not differentiate U_t. Boundary layers
can only improve it. Combining (10) with either (11) or (13) gives an actual
lower comparison envelope. In particular, if k_t=h_t log B/(M j_t),

    v(t)>=chi_t(-k_t)/M_t-t^2.                        (14)

No raw-depth rate is inferred without controlling the scalar inverse chi_t.
For example, a separately established lower Lipschitz bound
H_t(q_2)-H_t(q_1)>=c_1(q_2-q_1) would give
chi_t(-k_t)>=chi_t(0)-k_t/c_1. Strict monotonicity alone is not that bound.

Here is an explicit first-order lower coefficient for an actual signed radial
path. Assume the bounded radial first-speed hypotheses of the audited uniform
shape-envelope theorem, with inward speed v_z(X), and take a_t=c t+o(t).
Write H_z(X)=n_z(X).(X-g_z)>0 at regular boundary points. The required
containment I_(t,z) subset K_z(t) implies the nonnegative first collar width
c H_z-v_z. The ordinary continuous-integrand radial shell formula gives

    liminf xi_t/t >= c_col,
    c_col=(1/M) sum_z integral_(boundary K_z)
                        log L(z,X) [v_z(X)-c H_z(X)] dS.        (15)

Indeed (13) reduces this to a FIXED continuous integrand, and the collar
integral divided by t tends to the integral with factor c H_z-v_z. The
reference extension differs from its old radial-boundary value by o(1),
uniformly; bounded radial shifts make its contribution o(t). Formula (15)
has no missing moving-parameter shell derivative.

## 4. Conditional first-order consequence, with the missing hypotheses visible

Here is one safe formulation when a separate geometric calculation provides
more information. Suppose, in addition to the foregoing hypotheses, that
uniformly for r in compact intervals,

    H_t(Q+t r)=t(A r+B)+o(t),          A>0,            (16)

and suppose the actual near-minimizers satisfy

    liminf xi_t/t>=c.                                (17)

For signed radial paths Section 3 supplies (17) with c=c_col. Then (9),
monotonicity, and evaluation at Q+t r prove

    liminf [Q_t(U_t)-Q]/t >= (c-B)/A.                 (18)

Indeed for every r<(c-B)/A, (16)--(17) force q_t>=Q+t r for all sufficiently
small t; let r increase. If M_t=M-tD+o(t), then

    liminf [v(t)-Q/M]/t
        >= [(c-B)/A+beta D]/M.                       (19)

If (16) is piecewise rather than linear, the same argument uses the increasing
limiting scalar function and its generalized inverse. There is no reason to
insert a single derivative at a supporting branch automatically.

The inverse expansion (16) is NOT a consequence of parameter continuity.
The lower collar estimate (17), however, IS available as (15) under the stated
radial path hypotheses. It is an inequality: uniform interior convergence
does not justify equality of moving-parameter shell derivatives. No minimax
exchange is used in either assertion.

## 5. Exact boundary-layer warning for shape differentiation

Take K=[0,1], L=1 and, for 0<t<1/2,

    c=1-log 2,
    U_t(x)=exp(c t) min(1,1/2+x/(2t)).                 (20)

Then U_t is positive concave, its logarithmic mean on K is zero, and U_t->L
uniformly on every fixed interior core and in logarithmic L1. It even has a
uniform positive lower bound. Nevertheless on the actual removed shell
R_t=[0,t] of the nested convex interval K_t=[t,1],

    integral_(R_t) log U_t = -c t+c t^2,
    lim_(t down 0) t^(-1) integral_(R_t)log U_t=-c.    (21)

Replacing the integrand by log L would give zero. On the retained interval,
U_t is exactly exp(c t), so its NEW logarithmic renormalization is exactly
one. This verifies both the shell calculation and its normalization effect.

This example refutes a uniform varying-parameter shell derivative based only
on the proved continuity topology. It does not claim that (20) are exact
optimizers of a moving-body problem, and it does not refute differentiability
under stronger hypotheses. It shows the precise extra uniformity that a proof
would have to supply.

## 6. Relation to the outside-support concavity theorem

The independent source
`candidate 4f875cf42fc6ba0a`
proves the following actual response statement under its explicit finite data:
for facet-constant additive signed velocities, positive proper coareas, and a
linear singleton contact budget, OUTSIDE supporting inverses are jointly
convex. Their equalized common loss is concave, and one joint hypograph
separator can be chosen with consistent effective coareas and allocations.
Finite contact minima preserve the concavity with the stated bookkeeping.
INSIDE supports retain a finite existential branch choice; they do not inherit
one common separator from this argument.

The stability theorem here removes NONE of those first-order hypotheses.
It can keep optimizing parameters close on interior marks, but gives neither
an O(t) parameter jet, a linear contact-budget derivative, facet-constant
physical velocities, nor removal of an inside-support coincidence. Its useful
role is to justify limiting optimizer localization and the comparisons above.
It cannot upgrade that finite-response theorem to a differentiable optimized
envelope by itself.

## 7. Exact homothety calibration

For one interval K=[0,1], L=1, source Y=1/2 and its uniform certificate row,
write b=epsilon/sqrt(12), with 0<b<1/2. The actual source depth is
Q=1/2+b. Contract the interval about Y by a factor r_t tending to one.
The new mass and covariance are r_t and r_t^2/12, and centroid energy is r_t.
For any scalar source parameter s near one,

    B_1(t,s)=r_t(1/2+b sqrt(s)),
    s_1(t,q)=[(q/r_t-1/2)/b]^2.

Take T_t to be precisely this contraction. There is no collar, hence xi_t=0.
The lower comparison gives chi_t(0)=r_t(1/2+b), and the admissible constant
parameter gives the matching upper comparison. Thus the optimized normalized
value stays exactly 1/2+b. This checks the mass, covariance, scalar inverse,
and collar normalizations against an actual family, not merely formal jets.

The companion checker
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_parameter_stability_and_value_envelopes_slab_recovery.py` passes 224
exact calibration checks, including (21) and this homothety family. It does
not substitute for the analytic convergence or inverse proofs.
